source.description:
金智娟1991年聯合報資料照

金智娟身著藍色上衣，坐在粉色柔和的背景前，面帶淡妝，髮型蓬鬆自然，展現出優雅而自信的氣質。照片右上角印有「UDN 時光」字樣，標示出這是聯合報系的歷史資料照。

1981年，金智娟以「娃娃」之名加入丘丘合唱團，憑藉《就在今夜》一曲迅速走紅，成為民歌時期的代表人物。她高亢沙啞的嗓音和假音技巧，使她被譽為台灣第一位女搖滾歌手，代表作包括《飄洋過海來看你》和《大雨》。結婚生子後曾淡出歌壇，後來轉型為廣播主持人，並在本世紀初多次復出演唱會，持續活躍於樂壇。

source.description:
Wa-Wa Promotional Cover

A close-up portrait of Taiwanese singer Wa-Wa (金智娟) showcases her distinctive short haircut with a top knot, large circular earrings, and a soft pink backdrop. The bold red and black typography reads “娃娃,” with the subtitle “WITH BOX – for teenage,” indicating a youthful pop release.

Hosted on LINE MUSIC’s Taiwanese site, this artwork promotes Wa-Wa’s albums and songs, aligning with the platform’s presentation of her music catalog. The minimalist styling and pastel tones emphasize a fresh, teenage-oriented aesthetic.

source.description:
想念娃娃 (Missing: The Best of Wa-Wa)

This album cover showcases a sepia portrait of Taiwanese singer Wa-Wa (金智娟) against a vibrant orange backdrop. The bilingual title "想念娃娃" and "Missing The best of Wa-Wa" is prominently displayed, along with Chinese taglines that celebrate her journey from early beginnings to her most heartfelt performances.

Phrases like "從丘丘的圍牆到娃娃金智娟" and "娃娃最深情的歌聲與感動" highlight her artistic growth and emotional depth. The overall design uses warm tones and clean typography to evoke nostalgia and honor her status as one of Taiwan’s most beloved artists.

金智娟薄荷綠西裝全身照

金智娟身著一套薄荷綠色西裝，內搭同色系印花襯衫與手套，站立於單色灰色背景前，雙手交疊於胸前，面帶淡雅微笑。西裝上點綴細緻裝飾，褲裝剪裁筆直，整體造型清新俐落，突顯她的時尚品味與自信氣質。

這張專業攝影照以簡潔背景襯托出服裝細節與人物神態，適合用於宣傳或時尚專題報導。

source.description:
Wawa Jin Zhijuan Live Concert Poster

A striking promotional image showcases Taiwanese rock-pop singer Jin Zhijuan, known by her stage name Wawa, poised confidently against a shimmering golden bokeh background. The large white lettering “WAWA LIVE CONCERT” is complemented by Chinese text “娃娃金智娟 演唱会,” clearly announcing her upcoming performance.

Jin Zhijuan rose to fame in the early 1980s as the lead vocalist of the Qiu Qiu Band, which helped modernize Taiwanese campus folk music into pop-rock.
